summary: Inamrinone (originally named amrinone; renamed to avoid confusion with amiodarone) is an IV bipyridine PDE-3 inhibitor with positive inotropic and vasodilator (inodilator) actions, used for short-term management of severe congestive heart failure not adequately responsive to digitalis, diuretics and vasodilators. Given as a 0.75 mg/kg loading bolus over 2-3 minutes followed by a 5-10 mcg/kg/min infusion, with total daily dose generally not exceeding ~10 mg/kg. Dose- and duration-related thrombocytopenia is the hallmark toxicity; hypotension, arrhythmias and hepatotoxicity also occur. The original brand Inocor is largely discontinued in the US and product availability is limited.
indications: Short-term management of severe congestive heart failure not adequately responsive to digitalis, diuretics and/or vasodilators
Used in patients who can be closely monitored and who have not responded adequately to conventional maintenance therapy

dosage.d: 0.75 mg/kg IV bolus given slowly over 2-3 minutes
dosage.n: An additional 0.75 mg/kg bolus may be given 30 min after starting therapy if needed

dosage.d: Continuous IV infusion 5-10 mcg/kg/min, titrated to clinical response
dosage.n: Total daily dose (loading plus infusion) should generally not exceed ~10 mg/kg

admin: IV use only; administer with hemodynamic and platelet monitoring
Give the loading bolus slowly over 2-3 minutes
Dilute in normal saline or half-normal saline only - DO NOT dilute in dextrose-containing solutions (slow chemical interaction over 24 h)
Drug may be injected into running dextrose infusion lines via a Y-connector or directly into tubing, but should not be premixed with dextrose diluents
Do NOT mix with furosemide - an immediate precipitate forms
Use diluted solutions within 24 hours; protect from light
Titrate infusion rate to hemodynamic response and blood pressure
moa: Inamrinone selectively inhibits phosphodiesterase-3 (PDE-3) in cardiac and vascular smooth muscle, reducing degradation of cyclic AMP. The resulting rise in intracellular cAMP increases calcium availability in cardiac myocytes, producing a positive inotropic effect, while in vascular smooth muscle it causes relaxation and vasodilation (reduced preload and afterload). The combined effect raises cardiac output and lowers filling pressures, independent of beta-adrenergic receptors and the Na/K-ATPase pump.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to inamrinone/amrinone or to bisulfites (formulations contain sodium metabisulfite)
Severe aortic or pulmonic valvular disease in lieu of surgical relief of the obstruction
relative: Hypertrophic obstructive states (may worsen outflow obstruction)
monitor: Platelet count - dose- and duration-related thrombocytopenia
Blood pressure and heart rate/rhythm during infusion
Fluid status, electrolytes (especially potassium) and renal/hepatic function

preg: Pregnancy category C (historical). Animal studies have shown some adverse effects and there are no adequate, well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is not known whether inamrinone is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the nursing infant, exercise caution; a decision should be made to discontinue nursing or the drug, taking into account its importance to the mother.
renal: Inamrinone and its metabolites are excreted renally and clearance is reduced in renal impairment, leading to accumulation. Reduce the infusion rate and titrate carefully with close monitoring.
hepatic: Hepatotoxicity, including elevated hepatic enzymes, has been reported, particularly with higher doses and prolonged infusion. Use with caution, monitor liver enzymes, and reduce dose or discontinue if significant enzyme elevation or signs of hepatotoxicity occur.

major: Furosemide - physical incompatibility; an immediate precipitate forms if mixed in the same line, do not co-administer through the same IV site
Disopyramide - concurrent use may cause excessive hypotension
moderate: Other vasodilators and antihypertensives - additive hypotension
Diuretics - excessive fluid/potassium loss may potentiate arrhythmias and hypotension
Other positive inotropes/catecholamines (e.g. dobutamine) - additive inotropic and arrhythmogenic effects (may be used together intentionally with monitoring)
minor: Digitalis glycosides - inamrinone provides additional inotropy; monitor for additive effects and arrhythmias
interactions.alcohol: Not relevant to short-term IV hospital administration.
interactions.diagnostics: Causes dose-related decline in platelet count; may elevate hepatic transaminases. Correct hypokalemia (from concurrent diuretics) before and during therapy to reduce arrhythmia risk.

rare: Ascites, hepatic dysfunction with prolonged use

monitoring: Platelet count - baseline and during therapy; reduce dose or stop if it falls significantly (e.g. below ~150,000/mm3 or a marked decline)
Continuous blood pressure and ECG/cardiac rhythm monitoring
Cardiac output and filling pressures where available; clinical signs of perfusion
Fluid balance and serum electrolytes (especially potassium)
Liver enzymes and renal function during prolonged infusion
counsel: This medicine is given only by IV infusion in a monitored hospital setting
Your blood pressure, heart rhythm and blood platelet count will be checked closely
Report any unusual bruising, bleeding or palpitations to the care team
The drug helps the heart pump more effectively and relaxes blood vessels for short-term support
Treatment duration is kept as short as possible to limit side effects
pk: Peak hemodynamic effect ~10 minutes after bolus
~3.6-5.8 h (longer in CHF and overdose); ~2-3 h in healthy subjects
Dose-dependent; effect persists ~30 min to ~2 h after a bolus
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from light; use diluted solution within 24 h
pearls: Amrinone was officially renamed INAMRINONE to avoid medication errors with amiodarone - it is the same agent; the original brand Inocor is largely discontinued and product availability is limited
Thrombocytopenia is the signature toxicity and is dose- and duration-related - check platelets and limit infusion duration
Do NOT dilute in dextrose-containing solutions - dilute in normal saline; a slow chemical reaction occurs in dextrose over 24 h
Do NOT mix with furosemide in the same line - an immediate precipitate forms
Acts independently of beta-receptors and digoxin's mechanism, so it adds inotropy in patients already on digitalis and is useful when beta-agonists are limited
missed: Not applicable as a take-home medication. Inamrinone is a continuous, clinician-administered IV infusion titrated to hemodynamic effect in a monitored setting, so the missed-dose concept does not apply; the infusion rate is adjusted by the treating team based on response.
overdose: Overdose may produce excessive hypotension and arrhythmias. There is no specific antidote. Reduce or stop the infusion, support blood pressure (fluids, vasopressors/circulatory support as needed) and manage arrhythmias; provide general supportive measures and monitor platelets and cardiac rhythm. The elimination half-life is prolonged in overdose.
